blockers:
- BLOCKER 1 (behavior): packages/runtime/src/cli/report.ts, ownerOf (about line 63-68) with normalized. A bold key line with no support counts as evidence. Run on the head: the block `evidence:\n**Handles errors:**\n**Other thing:**\nchecks: ok` is accepted for both blocking criteria, with support `**`. The cause is that `entry.slice(at+1).trim()` is only checked for non-empty and emphasis marks are not stripped from the support. `- Handles errors: **` is accepted the same way. The old code and the doc comment say an entry that is only a key claims nothing. This weakens the acceptance gate, whose job is to refuse a missing blocking criterion. Fix: treat a support that is empty after stripping emphasis marks, backticks and punctuation (the LEADING and TRAILING sets) as no support. Add a test for it.
- BLOCKER 2 (behavior): packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts, the `hook commit-msg` command (about lines 735-762). It runs the phrase check over the whole message file. Under `git commit -v` or `commit.verbose=true` git puts the staged diff after the `# ---- >8 ----` scissors line, and the `#` filter does not drop diff lines. Run: a file holding `fix: x`, a scissors line and a diff line `+use the user setting` exits 3 with MessageRefused "the user". lefthook.yml wires this hook to every commit, and this repository's own instruction and doc text says "the user" often, so a clean message is refused. Fix: cut the text at the scissors line (and honour core.commentChar) before cleanMessage and forbiddenPhrases, and write back only the part above it. No test covers this.
notes:
- Baseline: none; mise run verify passed on 841ef47 with 683 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, and type-check, lint and format clean.
- Claim 1, normalized matching cannot accept evidence for a different criterion: held. An entry head must equal a declared key after normalizing case, spacing, trailing punctuation, a leading [blocking] and a trailing (dimension). `Handles error: z` and `Other thing: Handles errors: x` do not credit 'Handles errors'. A nested `B: x` line under A merges into A's support and is not credited to B. Only residual: two criteria that differ only by case, punctuation or a (dimension) suffix collide in `known`, so the second can never be satisfied. That fails closed, so it is optional.
- Claim 2, force-push detection: run over 36 forms. Denied: -f, -C dir, +main, +refs/..., env X=1, FOO=1, sudo, command, nice, xargs, time, exec, git -c, --no-pager, bash -c '...', (subshell), cd x &&, -uf, --force-with-lease=ref:sha, quoted '-f' and $'-f'. Allowed (correct): plain push, `HEAD:+main` (not a force in git), -o force. Misses are out of the stated scope or deletion-type pushes: `eval '...'`, `$G push -f`, `git push origin :main`, --delete, --mirror. Those last three rewrite remote history without a force flag. That follows the user's decision (only force pushes are denied), but the root should know. `git push -- -f` is a harmless false positive. No easy false negative inside scope.
- Claim 3, vcs commit stages exactly the named paths: held. `gitPaths(['add','-A'], scope)` uses --literal-pathspecs, and anything already staged outside declared paths plus Intent state refuses with StagedOutsideScope. Only the Intent-state fallback widens it. With no Intent in use, `changedIntentState` stages the changed files of the whole .holyagent/intents folder, including other open Intents with Running work. That is a behavior change from the base, which added nothing. Optional, and a root decision whether it matches 'Intent state in Git'.
- Optional, from the code-review run (read and confirmed in code): (a) `closeAssignment` accepts any `close --outcome success` on a Succeeded unaccepted Assignment and overwrites `result`, so an accidental duplicate close silently replaces the report. `assignment accept --report` also reaches the Running path and closes it as Succeeded. (b) `requireOwnIdentity` reads only `git config user.name/email`, not GIT_AUTHOR_*/EMAIL env, and `looksLikeAgent` duplicates `namesAgent` in vcs/message.ts with a narrower rule (exact noreply@anthropic.com versus any @anthropic.com). (c) `main.ts` calls process.exit(0) on EPIPE even when the run's result was a failure; the exit code is lost when a reader closes early. (d) `JsonReport` now accepts any extra field, which removes onExcessProperty strictness at that boundary. This is the requested behavior (extra fields kept), documented in the code, but it conflicts in letter with the CLAUDE.md schema rule. (e) `hook commit-msg` is not `stateless` and reads .holyagent/config.json through readSettings, so a malformed vcs section blocks every commit. Plain `git commit` already fails in the git-ownership cases, and I ran the hook in a temp repo without .holyagent: it works.
- I did not run mise run build to check that dist matches the sources. I only grepped dist/scripts/holyagent.js for force-push and hook commit-msg (both present). Lefthook commit-msg wiring was read, not run through lefthook. Tree status was clean at HEAD 841ef47 and no files changed during the review.
